chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding four men who looked down into the lion's pit. One of them fell, then he clung to the second, the second clung to the third, and the third clung to the fourth. So he judged the first to be the lion's prey, and imposed upon his family one-third of the blood-money for the family of the second, and imposed upon the second, for the family of the third, two-thirds of the blood-money, and imposed upon the third, for the family of the fourth, the full blood-money.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood-money; financial compensation due for wrongful killing
key_terms.زُبْيَةِ: a pit or trap dug for a lion
key_terms.فَرِيسَةَ: prey; the one deemed to have been killed directly by the lion
key_terms.قَضَى: gave a judicial ruling or judgment

ai.seo_question: How did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام rule on shared liability when several people caused one another to fall into danger?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal judgment of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning shared liability in a fatal incident involving multiple persons. It illustrates proportional responsibility in cases of intertwined causation and is significant in discussions of jinayat and judicial rulings in Shia fiqh.
